input.summary:
First-floor stair hall furnished in parts/room-4.mjs: a spruce-stair settle facing east with a fence-and-slab table, a barrel store at the south-west corner, and four hanging lanterns (min light 8, no dark cells).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes for this part; `mcd room` says OK.
The north strip x5..8 z7..12 (18 cells) is walk-unreachable from the arrival because the stair well and flight 2's steps cut it off. I left it bare and noted it in plan.md Notes.
left: North strip x5..8 z7..12 (18 floor cells) is not walk-reachable from the stair arrival: the well at x7..8 z10..15 and flight 2's steps at x5..6 z12..15 cut it off, and the living-room door x9 z12 opens onto the well. The room is furnished only on the reachable cells; the stair joiner or the plan needs a landing or bridge at y14 over the well.
The room.png render was a small overhead view; I looked at it once and did not refine the furniture beyond the settle, table, barrels and lanterns.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which floor cells were walkable from the plan grid, where ' ' (well) and 'o' (stair and rail) were ambiguous; the north-strip cut-off only showed after the first make and room check.
waste.cost: one make.sh cycle plus a room check, and a re-read of flight 2 and the well coordinates from the spec
waste.tool: `mcd plan --rooms` could print reachability from the entrance (the same flood `mcd walk` uses) and a legend for ' ' (well or hole), so cut-off cells show before any furniture is drawn.

waste.what: Drew the furniture layers as text with layers() but laid out each y-level by hand, and placed the table top as a second layers() call for y15.
waste.cost: about 6 rows of hand-typed characters and one extra call; coordinate bookkeeping for the stair cells was done by reasoning
waste.tool: a `furnish` helper taking a per-y legend of furniture in room coordinates, that checks each cell against the plan grid and the walk before writing.

waste.what: Looked at the render with one view from above, which is too small to judge the furniture at this scale.
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --tiles` or a zoom centred on the room's floor at a larger scale.

companions.task: Give the stairwell well and flight 2's foot a landing or a bridge at y14, so the north strip x5..8 z7..12 is reachable from the arrival and the living-room door at x9 z12 is no longer over the hole.
Check the light plan for the north strip once it is reachable, so the lanterns I hung there (x6 z9, x8 z13) are the right spots and the strip stays lit.

structured_output.summary:
First-floor stair hall furnished in parts/room-4.mjs: a spruce-stair settle facing east with a fence-and-slab table, a barrel store at the south-west corner, and four hanging lanterns (min light 8, no dark cells).
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE writes for this part; `mcd room` says OK.
The north strip x5..8 z7..12 (18 cells) is walk-unreachable from the arrival because the stair well and flight 2's steps cut it off. I left it bare and noted it in plan.md Notes.
left: North strip x5..8 z7..12 (18 floor cells) is not walk-reachable from the stair arrival: the well at x7..8 z10..15 and flight 2's steps at x5..6 z12..15 cut it off, and the living-room door x9 z12 opens onto the well. The room is furnished only on the reachable cells; the stair joiner or the plan needs a landing or bridge at y14 over the well.
The room.png render was a small overhead view; I looked at it once and did not refine the furniture beyond the settle, table, barrels and lanterns.

waste.what: Worked out by hand which floor cells were walkable from the plan grid, where ' ' (well) and 'o' (stair and rail) were ambiguous; the north-strip cut-off only showed after the first make and room check.
waste.cost: one make.sh cycle plus a room check, and a re-read of flight 2 and the well coordinates from the spec
waste.tool: `mcd plan --rooms` could print reachability from the entrance (the same flood `mcd walk` uses) and a legend for ' ' (well or hole), so cut-off cells show before any furniture is drawn.

waste.what: Drew the furniture layers as text with layers() but laid out each y-level by hand, and placed the table top as a second layers() call for y15.
waste.cost: about 6 rows of hand-typed characters and one extra call; coordinate bookkeeping for the stair cells was done by reasoning
waste.tool: a `furnish` helper taking a per-y legend of furniture in room coordinates, that checks each cell against the plan grid and the walk before writing.

waste.what: Looked at the render with one view from above, which is too small to judge the furniture at this scale.
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --tiles` or a zoom centred on the room's floor at a larger scale.

companions.task: Give the stairwell well and flight 2's foot a landing or a bridge at y14, so the north strip x5..8 z7..12 is reachable from the arrival and the living-room door at x9 z12 is no longer over the hole.
Check the light plan for the north strip once it is reachable, so the lanterns I hung there (x6 z9, x8 z13) are the right spots and the strip stays lit.
